newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Late profit-taking on the back of weaker U.S. Treasuries following the release of bearish economic data saw South African bond yields on the cusp of the key 15 percent level in late afternoon trade.
Dealers said it had been a volatile day with yields drifting in a 14.91 to 14.99 percent range before finaly settling just below 15 percent at the close.
At 1409 GMT the yield on the benchmark R150 bond was at 14.990 percent from 14.975 percent late on Wednesday.

The market saw some early strength but drifted slightly weaker despite the release of better-than-expected local August consumer price inflation data which came in at 7.5 percent year-on-year against a forecast 7.7 percent and 7.1 percent in July.
"Immediatley after the CPI release we saw some strength but selling shortly afterwards saw yields drift higher," a trader said.
He said there had been a good mix of mainly local buying and selling on the day and the late kick-up had been "purely on the back of profit-taking on U.S. rates".
U.S. weekly jobless claims and housing stats data came in more bearish than expected, sending the 30-year T-bond to a yield of 7.06 percent from 7.01 percent before the data was released.

"The market came off too quickly over the last week and will likely trade around the 15 percent figure for a while. But with money market rates having come off today (Thursday) and the money market shortage holding below eight billion rand the outlook is bullish," the dealer added.
Others said moves on the U.S. market would be important ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve Open market committee meeting on September 24 but also noted bullish local fundamentals.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of South African bonds for the second day running this week, purchasing 60.32 million rand worth on Wednesday after a net buying position of 384.62 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were 5.38 billion rand on Wednesday from 4.79 bilion rand on Tuesday.
The rand ended mildly firmer on the dollar but dealers expressed dissapointment that the unit had not managed to decisively breach the key 4.48 level on the downside.
At 1409 GMT the rand was at 4.4820/4870 on the dollar from 4.4850/4900 overnight after briefly walking a tightrope at the 4.48 level in the afternoon.

"The day was characterised by some good offshore dollar selling which should have broken the 4.48 level...it's dissapointing that we are back in the 4.48 to 4.49 range again," a chief dealer commented.
The bias was towards more strength and currency traders quoted the 4.45 level as the next crucual one on the downside once 4.48 was broken.
One dealer noted that volumes traded over the last while had been "constant but small," saying they were still too small for any major break to happen.
Against the crosses, the currency was at 6.9533/9655 against sterling from 6.9984/7.0093 overnight and at 0.3369/3375 marks from 0.3358/3364 marks previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs drifted lower to between 15.70 to 15.90 percent from 15.80 to 15.95 percent while 90-day BAs also fell to between 15.15 to 15.35 percent from 15.20 to 15.40 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the daily shortage at 7.589 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.315 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
